results.label: net.tcp.lifetime
degradations: `comm` and `pid` are the task current when the connection reached TCP_CLOSE, which is the closing process when an application closed it and is not the connection's owner when the kernel closed it from a timer or on a reset
10 of 20 connections carry no inode: a socket taken off a listen queue has no file, and therefore no inode, until `accept()` gives it one -- which is after it is established and is where this reads

20 of 20 connections carry no socket key: the kernel generates a socket cookie the first time something asks for one, and nothing ever asked for theirs, so they cannot be joined to `net.tcp.rtt` -- their inode is on the event instead
1 connection was still established when the run ended; their lifetimes have no end yet and are in no event
the filter kept 20 connections and removed 2; it ran here, over the drained records, not in the kernel

overhead.observed_from: everything but idle on every cpu (/proc/stat)
overhead.in_target_from: the kernel is not timing eBPF programs on this run: `kernel.bpf_stats_enabled` is 0, and BPF_ENABLE_STATS was refused (EPERM: it needs CAP_SYS_ADMIN); `sysctl kernel.bpf_stats_enabled=1` before the run makes what the programs spend inside the target measurable
